newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas supported by storage refills.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas supported by storage refills.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were mostly steady Friday as storage injections continued at a hefty pace ahead of the weekend, sources said.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub held at C$1.45-1.47 per gigajoule, while August AECO also remained flat at C$1.43-1.44.

"It's a pretty stable market. Field receipts (on NOVA) are at 12.4 bcf, and injections are high," one Calgary-based trader said, noting about 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas was injected into storage on Thursday.

The increase in storage refills was likely prompted by the cooler weather now in Calgary, where temperature highs are expected to hover in the low-70s F this weekend but then return to the mid-to-high 70s F early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
According to Canadian Gas Association (CGA), gas stocks in the West were at 138.36 bcf last week, or 53.9 percent full, versus 56.6 percent a year ago.
At Sumas, Wash., prices were little changed at $1.08 per million British thermal units in light trade.
In the East, prices at Niagara eased by about one cent to $2.32 in response to a mild correction on NYMEX and softer New York city-gate prices, traders said.

Gas stocks in the East wre at 100.12 bcf, or 43.1 percent full, compared with 44 percent a year ago, according to CGA. Overall stocks were at 238.47 bcf, or 48.7 percent. Last year, Canadian stocks had reached 50.8 percent of capacity.
